Done. `job.sbatch` is written, executable, and passes a `bash -n` syntax check.

```bash
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --job-name=sim
#SBATCH --nodes=4
#SBATCH --ntasks-per-node=32
#SBATCH --time=2:00:00
#SBATCH --partition=compute

./sim
```

Each requested clause maps to a directive: 4 nodes (`--nodes=4`), 32 tasks per node (`--ntasks-per-node=32`, i.e. 128 total), 2 hours (`--time=2:00:00`), partition compute (`--partition=compute`). The `slurm-jobs` skill was skipped since it only covers submitting a finished script via the Slurm MCP server; this workspace has no such submission step attached. The script has not been submitted anywhere and `./sim` was not run.
